sections.html:
Kane County deeds are recorded with the Kane County Recorder at 719 S. Batavia Avenue, Building C, Geneva, IL 60134. The phone is (630) 232-5935. The office's website, kanecountyrecorder.net, carries the price schedule, a land records search, forms and an eRecording page.

Before you head to Geneva, bring the signed and notarized deed, the filled-in transfer declaration, a check for the recording fee and any transfer tax, and a note of the parcel number. Staff will stamp the document and give it a document number. The grantor's postcard follows by mail, and the deed shows up in the land records search soon after.

A deed for a house in Aurora, Elgin, Batavia, St. Charles or any smaller village goes to that same Geneva office. Recording puts the new owner on the public record, and the title company or attorney at your closing normally handles it. If you are conveying without a title company, as in a family transfer, read the filing rules below before you go to the counter.

The county has about 195,957 housing units, and occupants own 76.0 percent of them. A typical owned home is worth $327,000. If a prior deed was never recorded, a title company or attorney can explain how to repair the chain before you list.

A standard real estate document costs $99.00 to record under the schedule effective October 1, 2024. A standard non real estate document costs $80.00. The schedule cites 55 ILCS 5/3-5018.1, the Illinois law that sets one predictable recording fee.

Kane County Recorder fees, schedule effective October 1, 2024

Plat of survey (one page, 11 x 17, up to two lots)$99.00

Fees are easiest to plan when you know the document type. A deed for a home sale is normally a standard real estate document, while a plat of survey or a condominium declaration is priced on its own line. Add up each document you plan to record and bring one payment for the total.

Pay with cash or a check made out to Kane County Recorder. Overpayments on checks are not returned. These fees cover recording only, and any Illinois transfer tax on a sale is a separate charge.

The GIS fee collected on every recorded document rose from $26 to $48 on October 1, 2024, after a cost study. The recorder keeps $1 and $47 goes to the GIS Fee Fund for the countywide mapping system. That increase is built into the $99 standard price, so a fee list from an earlier closing will show a lower number. Pull the current schedule before you write a check.

sections.h2: Why a deed is called non-conforming
sections.html:
A document that breaks the state's standard form rules pays the non-conforming price of $121.00 instead of $99.00. The standards are easy to check before you print.

  • Loose letter-size sheets (8.5 by 11), never permanently bound or on a continuous form. Graphics up to 11 by 17 record at no added charge.
  • Legible black ink, by hand, type or computer. Signatures and dates may be in contrasting colors if they reproduce clearly.
  • Plain white stock, 20-pound or heavier, with a half inch of clear margin all around.
  • A 3 by 5 inch blank patch at the top right of page one, left open for the recorder's stamp.
  • Nothing stapled or otherwise attached to any page.

More than five parcel numbers, or more than five referenced document numbers, on one document also brings the non-conforming price. A rejected deed costs you a second trip, so fix these points before you leave home. If you are unsure about a form, a title company or attorney can check it first, and a cash sale does not change any of these rules.

Illinois charges 50 cents for each $500 of value, or part of $500, and the recorder collects it under 35 ILCS 200/31-15. Paper revenue stamps are gone, so counties now issue electronic stamps or another marker.

Each recorded sale is also reported to the Illinois Department of Revenue through its MyDec system, with or without a stamp. That filing is the transfer declaration the recorder asks for along with a deed. Section 31-45 exempts certain deeds from the tax, including tax deeds, deeds that release security for a debt, deeds with consideration under $100, and deeds to a mortgage holder after foreclosure or in lieu of it. Some of those still need the declaration filed.

Kane County takes electronic recording through three approved vendors: Corporation Service Company, Simplifile and Hopdox. Contact a vendor to compare prices and enroll. Paper documents are scanned into the recording system, and plats cannot be sent through eRecording.

Electronic filing cuts processing to minutes, reduces rejections for wrong fees, and lets a corrected document be resubmitted in hours instead of days. Title companies and law offices usually use these vendors. A one-time family transfer usually goes to the Geneva office on paper with the correct fee.

The recorder's website has a free Land Records Search. The office also mails a green Property Transfer Notification postcard to the grantor whenever a deed is recorded. It shows a document number and a number to call if the owner did not know about the transaction. No sign-up is needed.

A seller can use the search as proof that the buyer's deed reached the record after closing, and an owner worried about deed fraud can watch for the postcard. The office also offers a Personal Information Redaction Request form and a Copy Center order form for copies sent by mail.

A photo copy is $1.00 a page. A certified copy is $80.00 through page four, plus $1.00 for every page after that. Plat copies run $5.00 for the first page and $2.00 a page after, with a certified plat copy at $10.00. A copy sent by fax or email costs $5.00 for page one and a dollar for each further page.

Military discharge papers get a break. A DD214 brought in by the veteran, the veteran's family or a VA representative is recorded free and includes four certified copies, while a commercial third party pays $80.00. A condominium declaration recorded with its plat is $149.00, with the map at $50 for the first page and $1 for each page after.

faqs.q: What is the fee for a Kane County deed?
faqs.a: Recording a standard real estate document costs $99.00 under the schedule effective October 1, 2024. A non-conforming document costs $121.00, and the recorder accepts cash or checks payable to Kane County Recorder.
Yes, through Corporation Service Company, Simplifile and Hopdox. Plats cannot be recorded electronically, and paper documents can still be brought to the recorder in Geneva.

faqs.q: What is the Illinois transfer tax rate?
faqs.a: The state collects 50 cents for every $500 of value or fraction of $500 under 35 ILCS 200/31-15. Ask the recorder about any local tax before closing, and expect to file the MyDec declaration.

faqs.q: Can I check that my deed was recorded?
faqs.a: Yes. Use the free Land Records Search on the recorder's website, or watch for the green transfer notification postcard mailed to the grantor after a deed is recorded.
Call the Kane County Recorder at (630) 232-5935 for the reason. An incorrect fee, staples, bound pages or no blank space on the first page are common causes.
